systematic_read.airway_lungs: CURRENT: Trachea roughly midline allowing for mild rotation. A linear tubular density projects over the tracheal air column, suspicious for an endotracheal tube. Low lung volumes. Diffuse bilateral hazy and coarse reticular opacity, most marked in the perihilar mid zones and both lower zones. Denser hazy opacity at the right base obscures the right hemidiaphragm. Hazy left lower zone and retrocardiac opacity. No pleural line seen, but the film is supine. PRIOR: Trachea central. Lungs well inflated. Mildly prominent right perihilar and infrahilar markings. No focal consolidation, no discrete nodule or mass. Vascular markings reach the chest wall.
systematic_read.mediastinum_hila: CURRENT: Upper mediastinum appears wide on a supine AP film, so width is not reliable. Hila are indistinct and partly obscured by perihilar opacity. PRIOR: Mediastinal contour unremarkable for a PA film apart from the enlarged heart. Hila not clearly enlarged. Left hilum partly overlain by the device generator and leads.
systematic_read.pleura: CURRENT: Right costophrenic angle and right hemidiaphragm are obscured by hazy basal opacity. Left costophrenic angle is hazy. A layering effusion on either side is not excluded on a supine film. No visible pleural line. PRIOR: Right costophrenic angle appears sharp. Left costophrenic angle is grossly clear. No pneumothorax.
systematic_read.heart: CURRENT: Cardiac silhouette appears enlarged. Size is not reliable on AP supine with low volumes. Borders are partly indistinct from adjacent lung opacity. PRIOR: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged on a PA film, with cardiothoracic ratio above one half by eye.
systematic_read.diaphragm_below: CURRENT: Both hemidiaphragms are elevated with low volumes. The right hemidiaphragm outline is obscured. Free gas cannot be assessed on a supine film. A tubular density projects over the upper abdomen in the midline, possibly an enteric tube or external tubing. PRIOR: Both domes are defined, right slightly higher than left. No free gas under the diaphragm.
systematic_read.bones_soft_tissue: CURRENT: No displaced rib fracture seen on this limited portable film. No soft tissue gas seen. PRIOR: No displaced rib fracture. No destructive bone lesion seen. Degenerative change at the shoulders. No soft tissue gas.
systematic_read.devices: CURRENT: Left chest wall cardiac device generator with transvenous leads. Coil segments project over the right mediastinal border (superior vena cava region) and over the lower heart (right ventricle region). Additional lead electrodes project over the left heart border, likely a coronary sinus lead. A lead with a curved tip projects over the right atrial region. Probable endotracheal tube over the trachea. Possible enteric tube over the upper abdomen. ECG electrodes are external. PRIOR: Same left chest wall generator and lead configuration: superior vena cava coil, right ventricular coil, and electrodes over the left heart border. No endotracheal or enteric tube.

findings.description: Hazy and coarse reticular perihilar opacity in the right mid zone, extending toward the upper and lower zones. Consistent with interstitial or alveolar fluid. Other diffuse airspace processes are not excluded.
findings.evidence: Prior PA shows only mildly prominent right perihilar markings with clear lung beyond. Current shows diffuse hazy reticular opacity out to the periphery. Supine position and low volumes add vascular crowding, but the opacity reaches the mid and upper zones, where low volumes explain less.

findings.description: Hazy and reticular perihilar opacity in the left mid zone, extending to the lower zone. It mirrors the right side.
findings.evidence: Prior PA shows a clear left mid zone apart from the overlying device. Current shows bilateral, roughly symmetric hazy opacity. Supine AP technique and low volumes contribute, but the bilateral perihilar pattern is denser than on the prior.

findings.description: Hazy opacity at the right base obscuring the right hemidiaphragm and costophrenic angle. Could be airspace opacity, atelectasis, layering pleural fluid, or a combination.
findings.evidence: Prior PA shows a clear right base with a sharp hemidiaphragm. On the current film the hemidiaphragm outline is lost. The current film is supine AP with low volumes, which crowds the bases and can mimic basal opacity.

findings.description: Hazy left lower zone and retrocardiac opacity with an indistinct left costophrenic angle.
findings.evidence: Prior PA shows a clear left lower zone lateral to the enlarged heart. Current shows hazy density at the left base. Low volumes, supine position and the enlarged heart shadow may account for some or all of it.

findings.description: Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both studies.
findings.evidence: Prior PA shows an enlarged heart. Current is AP supine with low volumes, which magnifies the heart shadow, so interval change in size cannot be judged.

findings.description: Linear tubular density over the tracheal air column, suspicious for an endotracheal tube. The tip appears to project above the expected level of the carina, but the carina is not clearly defined.
findings.evidence: No tube projects over the trachea on the prior. On the current film a vertical tubular density overlies the midline trachea at the thoracic inlet. The tip position needs confirmation by the radiologist.

findings.description: Left chest wall cardiac device (defibrillator-type generator) with a superior vena cava coil, a right ventricular coil, electrodes over the left heart border likely in the coronary sinus, and a lead tip over the right atrial region.
findings.evidence: The generator and lead configuration are the same on both studies. The differences in apparent generator size and lead projection are in keeping with AP magnification and supine positioning. No lead discontinuity is seen at this resolution.

cant_determine.recommend: Upright or semi-erect film or decubitus views when the patient is able, or bedside ultrasound or CT chest.

cant_determine.recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or echocardiography or CT as clinically appropriate.

cant_determine.recommend: Repeat upright PA film when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.

cant_determine.question: Is the right basal opacity consolidation, atelectasis or layering fluid?

cant_determine.reason: On a supine film air collects anteriorly and at the bases, and may not produce a visible pleural line. None is seen, but the film does not exclude it.
cant_determine.recommend: Upright film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.

cant_determine.reason: The image is low resolution and the carina is not clearly defined. A tubular density over the upper abdomen could be an enteric tube or external tubing.
cant_determine.recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Repeat the film if the tube positions remain unclear.

cant_determine.question: Is there free gas under the diaphragm?
cant_determine.reason: A supine film does not show subdiaphragmatic free gas reliably.
cant_determine.recommend: Upright or left lateral decubitus film, or CT, if there is clinical concern.

cant_determine.reason: The device generator overlies the left upper and mid zones on both films. Diffuse opacity and portable technique on the current film hide fine detail.
cant_determine.recommend: CT chest if clinically indicated. Review source images in PACS.

response.limits: Blind read of two frontal chest radiographs with no indication or dates. Prior is PA. Current is AP supine portable with low lung volumes. Projection, position and inspiration all differ, so comparison is limited and no size change is reported for the heart, the mediastinum or any opacity. The images are downsampled, so fine detail (lead integrity, tube tips, small nodules, subtle fractures) needs review on the source images in PACS. The device generator obscures part of the left lung on both studies. No lateral view. This is a draft for resident and attending review.
